only the licence plate format suggests a country; a plate is not evidence

notes: The file is 4317 px wide. At 768 px the octagon badge and the '1600 MkII' script are not legible, so the make counts only if 'MG' is read; the plate is legible and must not be transcribed.

history.change: expected "Classic roadster" pattern "(classic|vintage|british|1950s|1960s) (sports car|roadster|convertible)|roadster|sports car" became "^(?:(?:a|the|red|classic|vintage|british|english|mid-century|1950s|1960s|open|two-seat(?:er)?)[ -])*(?:sports cars?|roadsters?|convertibles?)$": the body type, with only describing words before it, and nothing else in the name
history.reason: The unanchored "roadster" alternative matched any name containing the word, so "MG MGA roadster" (a make and model read off the shape; the label accepts MGA only when "MG" is read) counted as a label-good claim and its correct drop as a clean drop (M4) in the golden-v2 blind run. A make or model name is now judged by the MGA entry and the forbidden makes, as the label intended.
